items.item: Portable electrical equipment, tools and flexible extension cords: construction site
items.reference: Model WHS Reg 163 (compliance with AS/NZS 3012:2019); AS/NZS 3012:2019; WorkSafe Vic Industry standard s.4.4 & Table 2
items.trigger: Inspect and test before first use; after repair; tag and record each test
items.who: Licensed electrician, licensed electrical inspector, or competent person trained in pass/fail PAT testing
items.jurisdiction_note: Model WHS jurisdictions (NSW, SA, TAS, ACT, NT, Cth; WA WHS (General) Regs 2022): r.163 makes AS/NZS 3012:2019 mandatory. QLD applies AS/NZS 3012 through the Electrical Safety Regulation 2013. VIC: the OHS Regulations 2017 contain no test-and-tag or RCD-testing regulation (no equivalent of model WHS r.150, r.163-165). The VIC benchmark is WorkSafe Victoria's Industry standard 'Electrical installations on construction sites' (Table 2); legal duty arises under OHS Act 2004 s.21 and OHS Regs r.114. VIC industry standard also requires 3-monthly test (earth continuity, insulation resistance per AS/NZS 3760).

items.item: Visual check of electrical equipment and leads before use: construction site
items.reference: AS/NZS 3012:2019; WorkSafe Vic Industry standard s.4.4
items.trigger: Withdraw and tag out if damaged
items.jurisdiction_note: Model WHS: via r.163/AS/NZS 3012. VIC: industry standard s.4.4 ('should be inspected for wear and mechanical damage').

items.item: Construction wiring including site switchboards and wiring in transportable structures (site sheds)
items.reference: AS/NZS 3012:2019 (via model WHS Reg 163); WorkSafe Vic Industry standard s.4.3 & Table 2
items.trigger: Initial test and certification before first use; re-inspect and re-test if a switchboard is relocated
items.who: Licensed electrician (VIC: A-class) or licensed electrical inspector
items.jurisdiction_note: VIC: industry standard s.4.3 - re-test every 6 months by A-class licensed electrician or electrical inspector; records on site. Model jurisdictions: 6-monthly visual inspection per AS/NZS 3012 (NT, TAS). Disagreement: SafeWork SA page lists 3 months for fixed/transportable equipment, construction wiring and switchboards - check site-specific requirement.
items.confidence_note: Regulator sources mostly agree on 6 months; SA page indicates 3 months.

items.item: RCD push-button test: portable RCDs (portable outlet assemblies/PSOAs, generators) - construction site
items.interval: After connecting to supply and at least daily when in use
items.reference: AS/NZS 3012:2019 (via model WHS Reg 163); WorkSafe Vic Industry standard s.4.5 & Table 2

items.jurisdiction_note: Consistent across VIC industry standard, TAS and NT guidance. Daily push-button tests need not be recorded (model WHS r.165(2)).

items.item: RCD push-button test: fixed RCDs on construction switchboards and site sheds

items.item: RCD operating-time (trip-time) test: fixed RCDs on construction switchboards
items.interval: Every month (VIC, up to 3 months if justified); every 12 months (AS/NZS 3012:2019 elsewhere)
